title: The Langlands research atlas
description: An editorial guide to concepts and proposed formalization tasks. Arrows suggest a learning and research order, not a proof dependency claim.

nodes.title: Number fields
nodes.summary: Finite extensions of the rational numbers provide the arithmetic setting. Start with their integers, prime ideals, and completions.

source.label: mathlib · Number fields and rings of integers

reference_source.label: mathlib · Number fields and rings of integers

nodes.title: Number fields
nodes.summary: Specify number fields and their rings of integers; isolate the ideal-theoretic lemmas needed by later statements.

source.label: mathlib · Number fields and rings of integers

reference_source.label: mathlib · Number fields and rings of integers

nodes.title: Local fields
nodes.summary: Completions let us study arithmetic one place at a time. The local viewpoint separates ramification and analytic behavior.

nodes.title: Local fields
nodes.summary: Record the completion, valuation, and residue-field hypotheses explicitly. Prove the required continuity lemmas.

nodes.title: Adeles & ideles
nodes.summary: Restricted products assemble the local pictures into one global object. The idele class group is a natural home for abelian reciprocity.

nodes.title: Adeles & ideles
nodes.summary: Choose restricted-product conventions and establish the topological group interface before stating global maps.

nodes.title: Class field theory
nodes.summary: Abelian extensions and arithmetic class groups are linked by reciprocity. This is a guiding case for more general correspondences.

nodes.title: Class field theory
nodes.summary: State a precise reciprocity map with its topology and normalization. Separate local and global target statements.

nodes.title: Galois representations
nodes.summary: Linear representations encode Galois symmetry. Their local restrictions carry information that can be compared with automorphic data.

nodes.title: Galois representations
nodes.summary: Fix coefficient fields, continuity, ramification, and equivalence of representations as explicit data.

nodes.title: L-functions
nodes.summary: Euler factors provide a common language for arithmetic and automorphic objects. Matching factors is one way to test a proposed correspondence.

nodes.title: L-functions
nodes.summary: Define unramified Euler factors first and make all exceptional places explicit. Keep analytic continuation a separate obligation.

nodes.title: Langlands reciprocity
nodes.summary: Seek precise correspondences between suitable Galois and automorphic data. The hypotheses depend on the field and the objects involved.

nodes.title: Langlands reciprocity
nodes.summary: Choose a sharply bounded case and state the matching conditions, including normalization of local factors.

nodes.title: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer
nodes.summary: The conjecture relates the rank of rational points on an elliptic curve to the order of vanishing of its L-function. It remains open in general.

nodes.title: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer
nodes.summary: Specify the base field and L-function, then separate the rank equality from the stronger leading-coefficient formula.

nodes.title: Reductive groups
nodes.summary: Reductive groups supply the symmetry objects of the program. Tori, roots, and parabolic subgroups organize their structure.

nodes.title: Reductive groups
nodes.summary: Agree on algebraic-group and root-datum interfaces, with each finiteness and field hypothesis stated.

nodes.title: Representation theory
nodes.summary: Representations turn symmetry into linear algebra. Local harmonic analysis asks how representations decompose and interact.

nodes.title: Representation theory
nodes.summary: Distinguish algebraic, smooth, and unitary representations. Build morphisms and equivalence without conflating the categories.

nodes.title: Dual groups & L-groups
nodes.summary: Dual root data and Galois actions lead to L-groups. They organize parameters and the expected transfers between groups.

nodes.title: Dual groups & L-groups
nodes.summary: Construct the dual root datum and state the required Galois action before defining the L-group.

nodes.title: Hecke operators
nodes.summary: Hecke operators expose arithmetic structure through eigenvalues. Their unramified theory connects representations to local parameters.

source.label: mathlib · Hecke rings and double cosets

reference_source.label: mathlib · Hecke rings and double cosets

nodes.title: Hecke operators
nodes.summary: Define the double-coset action and verify well-definedness and composition for the chosen space.

source.label: mathlib · Hecke rings and double cosets

reference_source.label: mathlib · Hecke rings and double cosets

nodes.title: Satake correspondence
nodes.summary: The unramified Satake picture relates a Hecke algebra to data of a dual group. It is an entry point to local parameters.

nodes.title: Satake correspondence
nodes.summary: Fix the group, compact subgroup, coefficient ring, and normalization before specifying an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Local Langlands
nodes.summary: Local correspondences compare representations of a group over a local field with suitable parameters. Cases and normalizations matter.

nodes.title: Local Langlands
nodes.summary: Select one local correspondence and enumerate its compatibility conditions; treat existence and uniqueness separately.

nodes.title: Functoriality
nodes.summary: Maps of L-groups predict transfers of automorphic representations. This is a central organizing principle of the program.

nodes.title: Functoriality
nodes.summary: Specify one L-group map and a transfer statement with matching local parameters at the relevant places.

nodes.title: Beyond endoscopy
nodes.summary: A research direction seeks to detect functorial transfers through spectral information. Analytic and structural obstacles remain.

nodes.title: Beyond endoscopy
nodes.summary: Extract one finite or bounded auxiliary statement; list all analytic estimates assumed by the proposed argument.

nodes.title: Harmonic analysis
nodes.summary: Integration and spectral decomposition make symmetry analyzable. Measures, topologies, and convergence are essential parts of each claim.

nodes.title: Harmonic analysis
nodes.summary: Establish measure normalization and the function spaces required by the intended integral identities.

nodes.title: Modular forms
nodes.summary: Holomorphic functions with modular transformation laws provide a concrete laboratory for automorphic ideas.

nodes.title: Modular forms
nodes.summary: Reuse available modular-form definitions where applicable and make cusp and growth conditions explicit.

nodes.title: Automorphic forms
nodes.summary: Automorphic forms extend the modular viewpoint to adelic quotients. Their transformation and growth conditions encode global structure.

nodes.title: Automorphic forms
nodes.summary: Specify the quotient, smoothness, central character, and growth assumptions of the chosen class of forms.

nodes.title: Automorphic representations
nodes.summary: An automorphic representation packages global harmonic data together with local components.

nodes.title: Automorphic representations
nodes.summary: State the ambient representation and the precise meaning of its local factors and restricted tensor product.

nodes.title: Trace formula
nodes.summary: Trace formulas relate geometric orbital data and spectral representation data. The precise identity depends on the chosen setting.

source.label: James Arthur · An Introduction to the Trace Formula

reference_source.label: James Arthur · An Introduction to the Trace Formula

nodes.title: Trace formula
nodes.summary: Begin with a controlled trace identity; expose convergence and truncation obligations before generalization.

reference_source.label: James Arthur · An Introduction to the Trace Formula

nodes.title: Endoscopy
nodes.summary: Endoscopic comparison isolates contributions that are difficult to separate by direct spectral analysis.

nodes.title: Endoscopy
nodes.summary: Record endoscopic data and transfer factors with fixed conventions; split matching from global comparison.

nodes.title: Fundamental lemma
nodes.summary: Ngô’s work established the Lie-algebra fundamental lemma using geometric methods. Here it is a reference theorem, not a checked artifact.

source.label: Ngô · The fundamental lemma for Lie algebras

reference_source.label: Ngô · The fundamental lemma for Lie algebras

nodes.title: Fundamental lemma
nodes.summary: Select an exact theorem statement from the reference and inventory the required geometry and integration machinery.

reference_source.label: Ngô · The fundamental lemma for Lie algebras

nodes.title: Stable trace formula
nodes.summary: Stabilization reorganizes trace-formula terms to support comparisons between groups.

source.label: James Arthur · The stable trace formula, §29

reference_source.label: James Arthur · The stable trace formula, §29

nodes.title: Stable trace formula
nodes.summary: Document which transfer results and normalization conventions a chosen comparison requires.

reference_source.label: James Arthur · The stable trace formula, §29

nodes.title: Algebraic geometry
nodes.summary: Schemes and morphisms supply a shared geometric language for families, arithmetic spaces, and cohomology.

nodes.title: Algebraic geometry
nodes.summary: Choose existing scheme interfaces and isolate the geometric properties needed by each later construction.

nodes.title: Elliptic curves
nodes.summary: Elliptic curves bring group structure to arithmetic geometry. Their rational points and reductions connect several branches of the map.

nodes.title: Elliptic curves
nodes.summary: Fix a Weierstrass model, nonsingularity, and the base field. Track changes of coordinates and the group law.

nodes.title: Étale cohomology
nodes.summary: Cohomology offers ways to extract arithmetic representations from geometric objects.

nodes.title: Étale cohomology
nodes.summary: Make the site, coefficient system, and functoriality requirements explicit before using cohomological constructions.

nodes.title: Shimura varieties
nodes.summary: Shimura varieties connect arithmetic geometry with automorphic phenomena and representation theory.

source.label: J. S. Milne · Introduction to Shimura Varieties

reference_source.label: J. S. Milne · Introduction to Shimura Varieties

nodes.title: Shimura varieties
nodes.summary: Choose a specific Shimura datum and level; list the canonical-model and cohomological inputs separately.

reference_source.label: J. S. Milne · Introduction to Shimura Varieties

nodes.title: Hitchin fibration
nodes.summary: The geometry of the Hitchin fibration is a key ingredient in Ngô’s approach to the fundamental lemma.

source.label: Ngô · The fundamental lemma for Lie algebras

reference_source.label: Ngô · The fundamental lemma for Lie algebras

nodes.title: Hitchin fibration
nodes.summary: Define the selected moduli problem and isolate a tractable fiber or support statement.

reference_source.label: Ngô · The fundamental lemma for Lie algebras

nodes.title: Modularity
nodes.summary: Wiles’s modularity work is a landmark bridge between elliptic curves, modular forms, and Galois representations.

source.label: Wiles · Modular elliptic curves and Fermat’s Last Theorem

reference_source.label: Wiles · Modular elliptic curves and Fermat’s Last Theorem

nodes.title: Modularity
nodes.summary: Distinguish the precise modularity theorem in the reference from broader generalizations and any unverified formal target.

reference_source.label: Wiles · Modular elliptic curves and Fermat’s Last Theorem

nodes.title: Geometric Langlands
nodes.summary: Geometric versions of the correspondence replace arithmetic objects with sheaf-theoretic and geometric data.

nodes.title: Geometric Langlands
nodes.summary: Select a specific version, curve, group, and sheaf theory. Record the scope before describing a conjecture or theorem.

nodes.title: Motivic connections
nodes.summary: Motivic viewpoints ask how different cohomological and arithmetic realizations reflect common structure.

nodes.title: Motivic connections
nodes.summary: Make the category and realization functors explicit. Keep conjectural properties visible as assumptions.
